subject: fitzroy river turtle
title: This Turtle Gets Most of Its Oxygen Through Its Rear End

scenes.text: This turtle breathes through its backside.
The Fitzroy River turtle, found in a single river system in Queensland, Australia. It can stay underwater for days.
Watch its rear end underwater: it pumps water in and out 15 to 60 times a minute.
Inside are two sacs lined with finger-like folds packed with blood vessels. They pull oxygen out of the water, like gills.
Up to about 70 percent of the oxygen it needs comes in this way. Other turtles must surface. This one hides on the river bed.
Breathing with your bottom sounds like a joke. For this turtle it is the whole survival plan.

description:
The Fitzroy River turtle takes in most of its oxygen through its cloaca.
This Australian turtle pumps water through its cloaca 15 to 60 times a minute into two sacs, called bursae, lined with blood-rich folds that absorb oxygen like gills. Researchers estimate it can get up to about 70 percent of its oxygen this way, which lets it stay submerged for days at a time. It lives only in the Fitzroy River system in Queensland.
Which animal has the strangest way of breathing?
first_comment: Hatchlings of this species can stay down even longer than adults relative to their size. What would you do with a day underwater?
